campingNotes: Halsviken: official/Naturkartan text says tenting is possible at the shelter/rest area.
Fjardbotten: official/Naturkartan text supports tenting and open cabin/rest facilities.
Horsang: off-route commercial camping/havsbad service reached by a signed side route.
GaviksTorpet: tents are possible around the guesthouse/farm area and at Strandstugan according to GaviksTorpet/Naturkartan, but this is private/commercial service.
Field reports describe Fjardbotten as a strong overnight stop; one report found Gaviksskatan poor for tenting and used Holsandsviken instead.
shelterNotes: Valkallen, Halsviken, Gronsviksfjarden, Fjardbotten and Lidenipan/Nipstugan are the main shelter/rest-cabin candidates.
Lidenipan/Nipstugan is the last under-roof overnight opportunity before the next section's Lappudden according to Naturkartan text.
ArkNat Stranded near Rodhallorna is promising but pending coordinate review.
fireNotes: Fireplaces/grill places are mentioned at Valkallen, Halsviken, Gronsviksfjarden, Fjardbotten and Lidenipan/Nipstugan.
Fire-ban status must override all fireplace records.
As of 2026-04-29, Lanstyrelsen Vasternorrland reported no fire ban in the county, but this is time-sensitive and must be checked again before publication/import.

dogs: General Swedish rule: dogs must not run loose in nature from 1 March to 20 August; outside that period they must remain under control.
No section-specific livestock or dog restriction was found in the first pass.
hunting: No section-specific hunting closure was found.
Use general hunting-season caution only: watch local signage, wear visible colors, and keep dogs close/leashed during active hunting periods.
forestryAndPrivateLand: No current forestry closure was found.
The route crosses managed/private rural land and local road sections; temporary forestry or storm-damage closures may only be visible on local signage or current app updates.
terrainSafety: Official difficulty is Svar / Rod - kravande and the section is a long day.
Valkallen side trip has steep sections with ropes near the summit.
Field reports mention rocky shoreline, rooty/rocky Lidenipan climbing/descent, mosquitoes, and wet-weather slowdown.
Field reports and official sources support generally good marking, but stale maps/old split labels can confuse route-app users.
waterReliability: STF warns water can be hard to find on Hoga Kustenleden, especially high summer.
Natural water and cold springs should be treated/filtered or boiled.
Lidenipan/Nipstugan explicitly has no drinking water.
One 2020 field report found water weak between the Horsang/Halsang road-junction area and Edsviken/Gavik; do not imply abundant water on the northern half.

conditionReports.summary: Recent reviews mention rocky shoreline, good signage, mosquitoes, steep stair/rope sections on the Valkallen side trip, and generally good/fair conditions. One 2025 review says no toilets, conflicting with official Halsviken/Fjardbotten facility sources.
conditionReports.importImpact: Keep toilet/facility records from official sources but flag verification/currentness.

conditionReports.summary: Recent reviews are mixed on scenic value and mention low traffic, long conifer-heavy walking, good views, no bathrooms, and route-app/signage alignment issues near road junctions.
conditionReports.importImpact: Do not suppress official facilities solely from user review; preserve stale-map caveat.

conditionReports.summary: Whole-trail review says maps/signs/AllTrails can disagree due to reroutes and old maps; water was generally findable but often from wells/taps/locals.
conditionReports.importImpact: Prefer latest official/Naturkartan geometry over old booklet/user tracks.

conditionReports.summary: Missed a turn toward Lovvik, filled water at a stream by Halsviken shelter, found Halsviken shaded, continued toward Norvarp/Rodhallorna, and describes boardwalks, some asphalt, and steep/hot Valkallen ascent with steps and rope.
Early spring report found much snow, a steady climb to Lidenipan and steep descent, scarce water after the Horsang/Halsang road junction until Edsviken, and poor tenting near Gaviksskatan.
conditionReports.confidence: high for early-season field experience; medium for currentness

conditionReports.summary: Describes hot conditions, rocky/rooty Lidenipan ascent, a shelter near the top, varied forest/lake/coastal terrain, recurring short road-walk sections, and about 13 km from Fjardbotten to Gavik.
Older field report supports Fjardbotten as a strong overnight stop with cottages, beds/tables, stove/fire and well/water, and Nipstugan/Lidenipan as a break point.

conditionReports.source: Reddit: 7-day High Coast Trail wild camping
conditionReports.reportDate: posted 2025-02-02; hike late spring before post
conditionReports.summary: Whole-trail report says markings were clear overall, Naturkartan water/service layers were useful, one public tap ran dry, streams were treated, and old booklet maps were confusing after trail updates.
Whole-trail thread notes rocky/rooty/downhill sections can be slow in rain and one hiker needed extra days in wet conditions.

researchIterations.summary: Overview pass established current 9-section trail structure, tested section 2 GPX availability, and identified the section 2 distance conflict.

agents.summary: Confirmed current identity, official stats, endpoints, official facilities/services, legacy split contamination, seasonal notes, and source contradictions.
Validated official GPX, Hoga Kusten embedded GPX, Naturkartan API linework, OSM relation 19096563, endpoint continuity and current/legacy merge assessment.
Collected facility candidates and coordinates for Valkallen, Halsviken, Gronsviksfjarden, Rodhallorna/Stranded, Fjardbotten, Horsang, Lidenipan and GaviksTorpet.
Verified Lovvik (KRF) start access, found no Gavik bus stop, selected Saltea (KRF) as closest practical end bus candidate, and documented parking/private-transfer metadata.
Reviewed AllTrails, blogs, Reddit, Komoot and Wikiloc for terrain, water, signage, old split naming, water-currentness, camping and condition caveats.
Checked protected-area/rule context, fire-ban status, dogs, hunting/forestry, water reliability, closures/reroutes and safety risks.

researchIterations.synthesisDecision: No extra agent batch needed before section handoff. Remaining issues are explicit import-time decisions or targeted map/currentness checks: distance selection, Gronsviksfjarden water status, Stranded coordinate choice, Fjardbotten cabin-count wording, and weak Gavik-end transit.

openQuestions: Verify Gronsviksfjarden water current status before importing as dependable potable water; Naturkartan still maps it but prior field evidence reported algae closure.
Avoid a hard Fjardbotten cabin count during normalization because current source text conflicts between three huts plus larger building and five fäbod huts.
Apply the side-trip POI policy from caveat-resolution.research.json to Valkallen, Rodhallorna, Horsang, Lidenipan viewpoint and similar detours.
If commute data is later imported from GTFS, replace DinTur/Fskab research stop ids and coordinates with authoritative Trafiklab/ResRobot stop ids and coordinates.
